title: Tabbi activity log day file (activity-record.v1)
description: One day of the activity log, as ActivityLogRepository (Sources/TabbiKitCore/Activity/ActivityLogRepository.swift) writes it: the file <edition storage>/Activity/<yyyy-MM-dd>.json, named after the local day (in the user's time zone) that each of its records ended on, holding ActivityRecord values (Sources/TabbiKitCore/Activity/ActivityRecord.swift) under the VersionedJSON wrapper. Streaks, the weekly recap, points and the pet all read these files. The Mac writes it pretty-printed with sorted keys, slashes escaped as \/ and a schemaVersion of 1; it reads files without schemaVersion (version 0, written before versions existed, which need no upgrade step), and files from newer builds as they are, ignoring keys it does not know. A file that is not valid JSON, or whose records do not decode, is refused as a whole and never overwritten. How records land in day files, the exact bytes written and how odd files read back are pinned by shared/fixtures/activity-log/activity-log.json.

schemaVersion.description: The VersionedJSON version of the day file. Missing means 0, which reads the same as 1.

records.description: Every record of the day, sorted by end, oldest first, at most one per id. Appending skips a record whose id is already in the file.

isoDate.description: An ISO 8601 internet date-time in UTC to the whole second, such as 2026-10-02T09:00:00Z. Records are made in whole seconds (a fraction rounds to the nearest second, half a second up), so a date reads back exactly. The Mac also reads a numeric offset (+02:00), but not a date without a zone or a number; never write fractional seconds.

activityRecord.description: One thing that happened: a focus stretch, a break, cards reviewed, a task done. Records are only ever appended.

id.description: A UUID, written in upper case. Reading accepts lower case too.

source.description: The module that logged it (a ModuleID), such as focus, study, anki, party or planner. Open: any string.

kind.description: What happened, an open id. Shared kinds: focus.completed (quantity is minutes focused), break.taken (quantity is minutes), cards.reviewed (quantity is cards), task.completed (subject is the task's id). Modules may log their own.

end.description: Never before start; equal to start for something that happened at one moment. The record counts toward the local day this falls on. Reading a file without it uses start, and an end before start reads as start.

quantity.description: How much, in unit. Left out when there is none (never null in a written file; null reads as absent).

unit.description: The unit of quantity, an open id: min for minutes, cards for cards. Left out when there is none.

subject.description: The stable id of what the record is about, such as a task's id. Left out when there is none.

metadata.description: Small module-defined details, always written (an empty object when there are none; missing or null reads as empty). Shared keys: outcome (completed, stopped, skipped or abandoned: how a focus stretch ended; completed and stopped count as finished sessions, and no outcome counts as finished), method (the study method, such as pomodoro), friends (a Party stay: how many friends studied along, as a decimal string).
